title: Logo Color Usage / Secondary and Limited Colorways
slide_intent: Separate broadly useful alternatives from restricted ones so expressive variety does not hide the logo.
strategic_value: Controlled secondary and limited palettes can give Burger King flexibility while acknowledging contrast differences.
demonstration: A left group of ten tiles presents secondary single-color treatments; a right group of six presents lower-contrast limited combinations.
practical_value: Choose a secondary treatment for harmony with type or images; reserve limited combinations for sparse out-of-home marketing and swag use.

reference_purposes.Intent: The secondary group supports harmony with typography or images; limited combinations are restrained because some have lower contrast.
reference_purposes.Expression: The tile groups demonstrate the permitted single-color and limited pairings.
reference_purposes.Application: Secondary treatments support applications and packaging where a single-color logo works better with other elements.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Limited colorways are used most rarely, sparingly, and only in out-of-home marketing and swag.

ingredient.name: Secondary and limited logo colorways
ingredient.role: Permit variation while preserving a readable signature.
ingredient.application: Use a secondary single-color logo when it better harmonizes with imagery or type; use limited combinations sparingly only for out-of-home marketing and swag.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 guide. Logo colorway groups are not identical to the primary/secondary palette groups defined later.
